question: Which remaining Linux companion app direction should OpenClaw pursue now that Windows Hub is shipped: C/GTK, Rust/GTK, another packaging path, or narrower Linux capability follow-ups?
rationale: The issue is no longer a simple missing-platform tracker: Windows is shipped, while Linux has multiple active implementations with different language, dependency, packaging, and security tradeoffs.

options.title: Choose a Linux app track
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers pick one Linux implementation path and ask competing PRs to converge or close.

options.title: Split Linux into narrower follow-ups
options.body: Close or narrow the umbrella only after creating canonical Linux issues for tray, notifications, pairing, packaging, and desktop capabilities.

options.title: Pause native Linux app work
options.body: Leave Linux on the supported Gateway-only path for now and close or archive the current app PRs as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Choose a Linux app track
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers pick one Linux implementation path and ask competing PRs to converge or close.

likelyOwner.reason: He opened the umbrella, provided product-direction comments in the discussion, and recently updated the platform status docs.
